title: NVDA Stock Bucks Selloff Premarket On SpaceX Boost, Foxconn’s Sales Update - Stocktwits
content: Nvidia Corp.’s stock rose nearly 2% in early premarket trading on Wednesday, bucking a selloff in the broader market and chipmakers, after SpaceX picked the chipmaker as its exclusive supplier of AI chips. CEO Elon Musk said SpaceX will build its AI infrastructure exclusively on Nvidia chips going forward. “Going forward, we’ve decided to build exclusively on Nvidia, because we think the Vera Rubin architecture is the best architecture. We think it’s the best AI computer, and we greatly value our close cooperation and partnership on many levels with Nvidia. We’re exclusive to Nvidia,” Musk said in SpaceX’s analyst call. If NVDA’s move holds in Wednesday’s regular session, it would be the fifth straight day of gains for the stock. Shares of AMD, SpaceX’s current chip supplier, fell 8% in premarket. Morningstar said the agreement could represent a retreat from plans to manufacture chips with Tesla through Terafab. Public documents released in May estimated that Terafab’s first phase would cost at least $55 billion, with a full buildout potentially reaching $119 billion. Intel joined the project in April, while Musk previously said SpaceX would lead its initial scaled-up phase. Meanwhile, Nvidia’s manufacturing partner, Hon Hai Precision Industry Co., reported a 54.2% increase in monthly sales, signaling sustained demand in global AI infrastructure buildout by customers. Revenue for July climbed to NT$946.5 billion ($29.3 billion), Hon Hai said Wednesday in a statement. Analysts on average are looking for a 31.2% increase in sales for the three-month period ending in September. The Nvidia server assembly partner said shipments of AI racks are expected to maintain momentum in the current quarter, while demand for information and communications technology products is entering peak season. Hon Hai, also known as Foxconn, booked a bigger-than-expected 40% jump in its revenue in the April-June period and has established itself as a key AI hardware player by assembling servers that house Nvidia accelerators. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for NVDA shifted to ‘bullish’ from ‘neutral', amid ‘high’ message volume. “$NVDA hopefully the rotation from AMD back into NVDA is starting,” a trader said. As of their last close, NVDA shares are up 13% year to date. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. “Big Short” investor Michael Burry on Tuesday said he sold off Microsoft shares, closed his short position in Oracle stock, and partially reduced his bearish bet in Palantir stock. Burry’s trades come just as Big Tech delivered a robust set of quarterly earnings.    Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet beat revenue and profit expectations, while the latter two also raised their capital expenditure forecasts for the year. Palantir, too, reported blowout results, which sent its stock up nearly 30% on Tuesday. Oracle has yet to announce the date for its quarterly results. Burry first disclosed a position in Microsoft in April and recently unwound it, according to a trading update on his Substack page. “That position benefitted from some lucky timing, and I cannot say my enthusiasm for Microsoft’s earnings report rose to the same level as that of the market,” Burry wrote. The Windows-maker issued a remarkably strong quarterly report last week. Revenue increased 19% in the company’s fiscal fourth quarter, with Azure Cloud and other services’ sales climbing 43% – both were above Wall Street’s projections at the time. The stock has soared over 25% in the four sessions since Microsoft issued the results. On the Oracle trade, Burry said, “These were the January 2027 low 100s strikes, and I decided not to roll them. The profit there was substantial, and so I left it at that. Should volatility come down, I may re-enter Oracle puts.” ORCL stock declined 11% in July, and got a lift this month. Burry has been one of the most vocal critics of Palantir, routinely flagging concerns with the company’s accounting and spending. He sold or let expire his January put options on PLTR, but kept his direct short position in stock. Palantir’s second-quarter sales nearly doubled to $1.94 billion, with U.S. commercial sales surging 149% and U.S. government sales rising 90%, according to results issued on Monday. The top and bottom lines comfortably beat expectations of $1.81 billion in revenue and EPS of $0.35. title: NVDA Reportedly Weighs Lower-Memory Rubin Ultra GPU Designs To Ease HBM Bottleneck — Why Retail Is Watching Micron - Stocktwits
content: Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) is reportedly testing multiple versions of its next-generation Rubin Ultra graphics processing unit (GPU), including designs with less high-bandwidth memory (HBM) than originally planned, as it evaluates ways to navigate potential supply constraints. The move reflects broader pressure on the semiconductor industry as soaring AI demand has strained the availability of advanced memory chips. The development has also sparked debate among Stocktwits retail traders over whether memory supplier Micron Technology (MU) could emerge as a key beneficiary if HBM shortages persist. NVDA shares were up 0.10% in Thursday afternoon trading at the time of writing. Over the past few weeks, Nvidia has been testing at least three versions of the Rubin Ultra GPU, some of which feature less memory than the company initially announced, reported The Information, citing people with knowledge of the trial. The company is considering the lower-memory designs in part because it may not be able to secure enough advanced memory chips to support its original configuration. While lower memory could affect performance, AI companies running large models on the reduced-memory versions may need to deploy more GPUs than they otherwise would, according to the report. CEO Jensen Huang unveiled the Rubin Ultra at Nvidia’s annual developer conference in 2025, saying each GPU would include 1TB of HBM4E memory spread across 16 memory stacks. Nvidia’s reported move shows how the AI boom has stretched the chip industry’s ability to meet surging data center demand. The resulting shortage of high-bandwidth memory chips has pushed up prices, increasing costs across the technology industry and forcing companies to spend more on hardware, according to The Information. The situation is notable because demand for Nvidia’s AI GPUs has itself contributed to the memory shortage, and the company is now exploring alternative memory configurations. The Rubin Ultra samples currently under evaluation would represent a reduction in memory compared with Nvidia's Rubin chip, which is already in mass production and being rolled out to customers. Stocktwits retail traders largely viewed the report as evidence that AI infrastructure demand is running up against real-world supply constraints, while debating the implications for Nvidia and memory chip suppliers. Micron entered the discussion as it is one of Nvidia’s suppliers of high-bandwidth memory used in the chipmaker’s AI GPUs. One retail trader said Nvidia’s reported testing of lower-memory Rubin Ultra GPUs suggests “supply constraints are real” even for the AI chip leader. The user added that less memory per chip could require more GPUs to run large AI models. The trader concluded by saying, “The AI buildout isn’t stopping. It’s just getting more complicated.” Another retail trader said the reported memory reduction shows that “supply crunch is real,” adding that while it could allow Nvidia to produce more GPUs, “MU is the real beneficiary here,” as AI infrastructure buildouts run into physical supply constraints. Shares of Moderna (MRNA) jumped 4% on Thursday morning before paring gains after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved mFLUSIVA, a seasonal influenza vaccine for adults 50 and older, validating its mRNA-based approach for uses beyond COVID treatment. At the time of writing, the stock pared some of the gains and was trading 3% lower. The approval makes mFLUSIVA Moderna’s fourth FDA-cleared product and the first messenger RNA-based flu vaccine. It is authorized for all adults aged 50 and up. For those 50-64, full approval rests on a large late-stage trial involving more than 40,000 people that compared it to a standard flu shot. For adults 65 and older, the FDA granted it accelerated approval, meaning the firm will conduct confirmatory studies to validate efficacy and ensure a full, traditional approval. CEO Stéphane Bancel called the decision proof of the mRNA platform’s strength. “Flu remains a significant public health challenge, and mFLUSIVA provides an important new option for America’s seniors,” he said. Moderna expects doses to reach select U.S. retailers in the coming weeks for the 2026-2027 season. It will sit alongside the company’s COVID-19 and Respiratory Syncytial Virus vaccines. The company is also seeking approval for the vaccine in the European Union, Canada, and Australia, with more filings planned this year. Moderna first filed for approval of the vaccine in December, but in February, the agency refused to review the application, citing the use of a regular flu shot for comparison instead of a stronger version preferred for seniors. Moderna quickly revised its request to seek full approval for ages 50–64 and a faster track for those 65 and older. The FDA accepted the updated filing within days and set an August decision date. After the COVID-19 pandemic propelled Moderna’s vaccine sales to a peak of more than $18 billion in 2022, demand collapsed, driving annual revenue down to roughly $1.9 billion by 2025. In response, the company sharply cut costs, reduced its workforce, and discontinued several early programs, while shifting strategy to build a steady seasonal respiratory franchise—including flu, RSV, and combination shots. The artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure spending boom is building at a pace unmatched by previous investment cycles, according to Apollo Chief Economist Torsten Slok, who warned that the rapid expansion could become a macroeconomic risk if AI demand eventually disappoints. In a note on Thursday, Slok said consensus forecasts imply hyperscaler capital expenditures will reach about 3% of U.S. Gross Domestic Product (GDP) annually between 2027 and 2029, up from 0.3% in 2019 and 1.4% in 2025. He argued that while the buildout remains smaller than the housing investment boom in absolute size, it is building at a much faster pace and could unwind just as quickly. Slok said hyperscaler capital expenditures are expected to rise from 0.6% of GDP in 2023 to 3.1% in 2027, representing a 2.5 percentage-point increase. By comparison, the late-1990s telecom buildout increased by 0.4 percentage points, while residential investment climbed 2.2 percentage points during the housing expansion that preceded the global financial crisis. He added that the AI buildout is accelerating at roughly 0.85 percentage points of GDP per year, compared with about 0.5 percentage points during the fastest phase of the housing boom and roughly 0.15 percentage points during the telecom investment cycle. “The AI cycle is building at close to twice the pace of the housing boom at its fastest,” Slok wrote. While hyperscaler capital spending is projected to exceed the peak of the late-1990s telecom and fiber buildout as a share of GDP, Slok noted it remains well below the 6.6% peak reached by residential investment in 2005. However, he argued that the speed of the expansion also increases the potential downside. “A cycle that builds at 0.85 percentage points a year can unwind at a similar pace, and that, rather than the buildout itself, is the macro risk if AI demand disappoints,” he said. Slok said previous investment cycles offer a useful benchmark for assessing today's AI infrastructure buildout. He noted that the collapse of the telecom and fiber spending boom in the early 2000s contributed to what he described as the mildest post-war recession. By contrast, the reversal in residential investment proved far more damaging. Residential investment fell from 6.2% of GDP in early 2006 to 3% by the end of 2008, a decline Slok said helped make the Global Financial Crisis recession significantly more severe. According to a Bloomberg report, the four big hyperscalers in the U.S., Alphabet Inc. (GOOG, GOOGL), Microsoft Corp. (MSFT), Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN), and Meta Platforms Inc. U.S. sales of Amtagvi, Iovance’s cell therapy for advanced melanoma, were around $91 million, while its immunotherapy Proleukin generated about $9 million in global revenue, with the company expecting sales to increase through the rest of the year. Interim President and CEO Frederick Vogt said the strong quarterly performance has prompted Iovance to review its previously issued 2026 revenue guidance of $350 million to $370 million, with an update expected during the third quarter. The company also expects gross margins, which came in at 56% in Q2, to continue improving. Iovance also highlighted progress across its next-generation immuno-oncology pipeline. The company is enrolling patients in early-stage trials of IOV-4001 for melanoma and non-small cell lung cancer, and IOV-5001, which is being studied in colorectal, breast and other solid tumors. The company is also expanding its studies of Lifileucel into new cancers, including cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma and Merkel cell carcinoma, with initial data expected in the first half of 2027. As of June 30, Iovance had $304 million in cash and expects it to fund operations through the second half of 2028. title: Nvidia In Correction Territory? Investors Parse Fresh Risks From Chinese Rival - Stocktwits
content: Nvidia Corp. shares have been a curious underperformer among major chip stocks lately. Last week's blowout earnings report did little to lift the stock, nor did an $80 billion buyback authorization or a dividend raise. In fact, CEO Jensen Huang went so far as to say that the stock move remains a “mystery” for him. Now, another risk appears to be weighing on the stock. On Monday, China’s Huawei discussed a new approach to developing advanced semiconductors that would enable it to produce vastly superior chips more quickly. Huawei’s LogicFolding approach improves chip performance by stacking computing blocks vertically, so data travels shorter distances within the processor, rather than relying mainly on shrinking transistors. Its approach is unique because Huawei is proposing a far more aggressive redesign of chip architecture and packaging to work around U.S. export restrictions and the limits of its manufacturing technology. Using LogicFolding, Huawei said it aims to produce semiconductors with performance comparable to 1.4nm chips by 2031. That would still leave Huawei years behind TSMC, which is targeting similar advances by 2028, but it would represent a substantially narrower gap than what exists today. Nvidia shares have dropped 10.1% from their peak of $236.54 on May 14, signaling that the stock has entered correction territory. Despite a sharp run-up last month, NVDA shares are up 14% this year, well below peers in the chip sector. Intel and Micron have risen 225% to 230%, while AMD is up 132% – pushing the sector’s benchmark, the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX), 87% higher. Last week, Nvidia reported blowout quarterly results, announced an $80 billion share buyback, and raised its dividend — moves that signaled strong financial health and underscored robust demand for AI chips. A battery of analysts raised their price targets on the NVDA, although the stock has only slid since then. On Wednesday, Tigress Financial raised its price target on Nvidia to $425 from $360, keeping a ‘Strong Buy’ rating on the shares. The target is double of NVDA’s last closing price. Nvidia continues to be "the core infrastructure engine of the AI factory era" and is the "must-own core holding for the AI investment cycle," the research firm said. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for NVDA dipped to ‘bullish’ on Wednesday night, from ‘extremely bullish’ the previous day. While the recent move remains unexplained and frustrating, traders argued that the stock would move higher eventually. “Nvidia is heavily investing billions of dollars in other companies, particularly focusing on AI infrastructure, startups, and data center technology to solidify its dominance. Have faith ... I'm buying the Jensen hedge fund,” a trader said. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Read Next: Why Is NBIS Stock Soaring Over 10% In Overnight Trading? Shares of Sellas Life Sciences Group (SLS) rose 2% in overnight trading heading into Thursday after CEO Angelos Stergiou said he is “very bullish” on upcoming Regal data that could potentially help push its flagship cancer drug GPS toward broader National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) recognition in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). SLS stock jumped 6% on Wednesday, on track for its fifth straight week of gains and its best month this year. Stergiou made the comments during TD Cowen’s 7th Annual Oncology Innovation Summit on Wednesday as investors focus on the company’s late-stage Regal trial, one of the biggest near-term catalysts for Sellas. The Phase 3 Regal study is evaluating galinpepimut-S (GPS), an immunotherapy targeting the WT1 cancer antigen, in AML patients who have achieved a second complete remission but are not eligible for stem cell transplant. The Regal study recently reached 78 out of 80 required events, with the 80th event serving as the trigger for final analysis and topline data disclosure. The CEO said at the summit that the study has continued significantly longer than initially projected, which investors interpret as a potentially positive sign for survival outcomes. “80 events have not occurred yet, almost 25 months after enrollment completion, which obviously indicates longer survival than projected,” Stergiou said. Stergiou reiterated that “every passing month” may improve the probability of a successful outcome due to a potential GPS effect. The company previously said the study was designed to show that GPS-treated patients could live longer than those receiving standard treatment, with a median overall survival projected at about 12.6 months versus 8 months in the control group. According to Stergiou, anything above a four-month survival difference would be considered “very clinically significant,” though he added the company hopes to see an even larger benefit. One of the most closely watched comments from the conference came when Stergiou said that positive Regal data could potentially support broader NCCN recognition for GPS beyond the current trial setting. “I would also expect, depending on the data that we will see, and what I believe is that there’s a good chance that the REGAL trial would show GPS to have a median survival very similar to what [we] showed in AML CR1, to get NCCN guidelines also in the CR1 setting,” Stergiou said. The CEO added, “We’re very bullish, but at the same time we’re very pragmatic.” Stergiou also said that GPS could emerge as a maintenance therapy option for AML patients after remission, noting that no therapies are currently approved for AML CR2 maintenance. Much of the TD Cowen discussion focused on earlier GPS data that continues fueling optimism ahead of the Phase 3 readout. Stergiou called the prior AML data “quite unprecedented” after Sellas reported a median overall survival of approximately 68 months in a Phase 2 study following first complete remission. In AML patients aged 60 and older, the company reported a median survival of 35.5 months. The CEO also pointed to earlier data in relapsed AML patients who achieved second remission, where GPS-treated patients showed a median survival of 21 months compared with 5.4 months for patients who did not receive the therapy. The latest comments also come after Stergiou discussed new real-world data involving elderly AML patients treated at MD Anderson Cancer Center in a LinkedIn post on Tuesday. According to the CEO, newer chemotherapy combinations are helping more elderly AML patients achieve remission, but most still fail to reach stem cell transplant. “Despite being touted as a ‘bridge to transplant,’ only 15% of these patients actually made it to an allogeneic stem cell transplant,” Stergiou said. “For the remaining 85% who are too frail or older, a steep therapeutic cliff remains.” The CEO used the findings to reinforce Sellas’ thesis around GPS and the unmet need in elderly AML maintenance therapy. Beyond GPS,  Sellas’ second AML program, SLS009, a highly selective CDK9 inhibitor currently in Phase 2 testing, is also gaining traction. During the TD Cowen summit, Stergiou contrasted SLS009 against earlier CDK9 programs from companies including AstraZeneca that were eventually discontinued. “Other programs, such as AstraZeneca, they are CDK9 inhibitors who discontinued their programs,” Stergiou said. “They are not as selective and specific to the CDK9 target as SLS009 is.” The CEO said SLS009 remains in the body “long enough to kill cancerous cells, but not long enough to cause severe toxicities.” Sellas expects topline SLS009 data later this year and said it may pursue accelerated approval depending on the results. Shares of AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) slipped over 2% in overnight trading heading into Thursday after fresh regulatory filings revealed that President Scott Wisniewski sold about $3.3 million worth of stock just as the company advanced its next BlueBird satellite launch campaign with SpaceX. ASTS stock jumped over 8% on Wednesday to end at $129.6, with shares on track to log their fourth straight week in the green. A new regulatory filing late Wednesday showed that Wisniewski sold 25,904 Class A shares at a weighted-average price of $126.64 per share through multiple transactions ranging from $126.41 to $126.99. The transaction was valued at $3.28 million. After the sale, Wisniewski still owns 745,973 shares of AST SpaceMobile stock. A separate filing also showed that the shares were granted as restricted stock units that vested on March 31, 2026, as part of executive compensation. The filing also disclosed that Wisniewski sold another 47,000 shares for $4.45 million on March 17. The insider sale came as AST SpaceMobile continued building momentum around its next satellite deployment campaign. In a recent post on X, the company said “Convoy complete,” confirming that BlueBird 9 had officially arrived at Cape Canaveral ahead of its next Falcon 9 launch campaign with SpaceX. “Built in Texas. Broadband from space. Designed to connect directly to everyday smartphones,” the company said. The latest update follows a string of recent operational milestones for AST’s Block 2 satellite rollout. Earlier this week, AST SpaceMobile confirmed that BlueBirds 8 and 10 had already arrived at Cape Canaveral while BlueBird 9 departed the company’s Midland, Texas, manufacturing facility. The satellites are expected to launch aboard a Falcon 9 rocket in a mid-June mission. AST said that the three commercial satellites have now entered final processing and integration at the Florida launch site after being transported from Texas. The updates appeared aimed at reassuring investors after concerns surfaced last month surrounding BlueBird 7, which failed to reach orbit following an upper-stage anomaly during Blue Origin’s New Glenn Mission-3 launch. The incident raised fresh questions about whether AST could maintain its aggressive deployment timeline. By successfully moving three new satellites to Florida on schedule, the company appears focused on showing that its manufacturing and launch pipeline remains intact despite recent setbacks. The BlueBird rollout also comes after CEO Abel Avellan recently reiterated the company’s target of deploying 45 satellites this year despite launch risks and increasing competition in the direct-to-device satellite market. During a recent CNBC interview, Avellan said AST remains “on target” and added that launches are expected “approximately every month.” “Today we're shipping in a batch of satellites in the launch pad,” Avellan said, while noting that AST works with multiple launch providers including SpaceX. Avellan also defended AST’s tech advantage in the direct-to-smartphone broadband race as competition intensifies from Starlink and other satellite connectivity players. “We are the only broadband system that is available in terms of technology to basically do hundreds of megabits per second directly to any device,” Avellan said. The CEO also pointed to AST’s previous demonstrations involving satellite voice calls, 5G connectivity and broadband transmissions directly to smartphones. He also said the company and its partners now control access to nearly 100 MHz of spectrum while AST holds more than 3,800 patents. Despite the recent operational progress, stakeholders are monitoring whether AST can scale launches quickly enough to support its long-term broadband ambitions. Satellite communications analyst Tim Farrar previously said that AST’s deployment assumptions likely require a heavy launch cadence involving both Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket and multiple Falcon 9 launches to achieve year-end targets. On the other hand, Wisniewski had signaled confidence by previously saying that AST expects “a handful” of launches from both Blue Origin and SpaceX, or equivalent providers, and believes the company has enough contracted launch capacity to meet its deployment roadmap. Shares of smaller space stocks soared on Wednesday after NASA outlined plans for near-monthly lunar missions starting in 2027. However, the rally came with a reality check from NASA chief Jared Isaacman, who cautioned that commercial demand in orbit remains uncertain. On Wednesday, Momentus (MNTS) jumped another 26% after more than doubling in the previous session, putting the stock on track for its best week since October 2023. Rocket One, formerly Hoth Therapeutics and set to begin trading under the ticker RKTO on Thursday, surged 92%, heading for its strongest weekly performance since January 2025. Meanwhile, Astrotech (ASTC) skyrocketed 459%, with the stock poised to log its biggest weekly gain on record. In an interview with Bloomberg on Wednesday, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman outlined a roadmap for expanding lunar operations, including near-monthly robotic missions to the Moon beginning in 2027 and long-term plans for permanent infrastructure on the lunar surface ahead of future Artemis astronaut landings. NASA expects to spend $20 billion over seven years, alongside commercial partners such as SpaceX and Blue Origin, with future phases involving cargo systems, autonomous infrastructure, heavier equipment deployments and eventually astronaut stays lasting months at a time during the early 2030s. However, Isaacman also warned that the orbital economy “has been grossly overstated,” saying that government agencies still remain the primary source of demand across much of the industry. He questioned whether enough sustainable commercial demand exists beyond government-backed programs, noting that NASA still cannot identify who would buy the “50th lunar lander” if not the government itself. Investor excitement around SpaceX’s expected IPO has also fueled momentum in the rally across space stocks. The Elon Musk-led company is reportedly targeting a $2 trillion valuation, potentially making it the first trillion-dollar IPO in U.S. history. Investors view SpaceX not only as a launch provider but as a long-term infrastructure and AI platform spanning satellite communications, defense systems, and orbital transportation. Publicly traded space companies could see renewed investor interest if SpaceX sustains its targeted valuation, which appears to be driven more by expectations around future orbital infrastructure demand than near-term profitability. Meanwhile, FTSE Russell also called for major changes to its IPO inclusion rules that would allow newly listed mega-cap companies to qualify for fast-track entry into major indexes after only five trading days. Based on current estimates, SpaceX would already qualify for rapid inclusion into several major benchmark indexes under the revised rules, potentially unlocking massive passive-fund inflows. Momentus has emerged as one of the market’s hottest recent space trades after former astronaut and Momentus director Chris Hadfield purchased 2,000 shares through his firm, Chris Hadfield Inc., at an average price of $7.19 per share last week. Hadfield, the former International Space Station commander widely known for recording David Bowie’s “Space Oddity” while in orbit, now holds 3,500 shares of the company. The insider purchase came shortly after Momentus filed a shelf registration, allowing the company to potentially raise up to $200 million through future securities offerings. On Wednesday, the company separately announced agreements with existing institutional investors to raise $25 million through a private placement of nearly 2.94 million shares. After the financing, Momentus said it expects to hold around $76 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments. The company operates in-space logistics and orbital transportation systems through its Vigoride Orbital Service Vehicle platform, which recently supported missions tied to NASA, DARPA and U.S. defense organizations aboard SpaceX’s Transporter-16 launch. On Wednesday, Astrotech said it is exploring future opportunities for moon-based resources and infrastructure, including extracting water from the lunar surface, processing rare materials such as helium-3 and silicon-28, and eventually supporting advanced chipmaking and quantum computing systems in space. The company said it believes the moon’s environment,  including lower gravity, constant solar energy in some regions and access to strategic raw materials, could one day make it suitable for building semiconductor, AI and computing infrastructure. Meanwhile, Hoth Therapeutics completed its rebrand to Rocket One Inc., shifting its focus toward orbital computing and defense tech under the ticker RKTO beginning May 28. Rocket One said it holds rights to nanomagnetic AI chip tech for radiation-tolerant and energy-constrained environments such as satellites, low-Earth orbit systems and deep-space platforms. The company said future space systems will depend on onboard AI processing capabilities that can operate independently in harsh orbital environments. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for MNTS, RKTO, and ASTC was ‘extremely bullish’ amid ‘extremely high’ message volume. One user said, “$ASTC actually the more I read on this stock the more it’s justifying the price, kinda low actually. This is insane future stuff!!!” Another user said, “$HOTH Space tech is so hot right now.  This is going to be lit tomorrow. Sleep tight bears.” Over the past year, ASTC soared 135%, RKTO, formerly HOTH, climbed 58%, while MNTS is still down 37% despite its recent rally. title: Prediction: $200 a Month Invested in Nvidia Will Be Worth This Much by 2035 - The Motley Fool
content: Small but steady investments in the chipmaker could build a meaningful position by 2035. Putting aside $200 to invest every month is not something everyone can do. Yet for those who can and do, the potential rewards are real. If you start next month and continue through December 2035, you'll have put aside $22,000 in contributions alone. But along the way, if you put that money into the right investments -- for example, Nvidia (NVDA -0.59%) -- those contributions could grow into a much larger nest egg. But what's a realistic return to expect from that strategy over the next nine years, especially given how much Nvidia stock has already grown recently? The answer starts with Nvidia's business model and ends with how much investors are willing to pay for its future. Imagine it's 2035. Artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots have moved from the fringes to everyday use. Scheduling an appointment? You'll almost certainly be talking to an AI chatbot. At the drive-thru? An AI chatbot might take your latte order. Have a question about your taxes? There will likely be an AI chatbot for that. In short, AI isn't going anywhere. In fact, as the systems improve, organizations will rely more on AI-powered tools to stay competitive and meet consumer expectations for speed, accuracy, and 24/7 availability. To power these applications, AI hyperscalers will need a far greater number of expensive graphics processing units (GPUs), the brains of the latest and greatest AI applications. Or as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang recently said, "AI has reached its inflection point." What Huang means by this is that AI systems are increasingly moving from learning about the world (training) to problem-solving (inference). As we move forward, these systems will be able to handle increasingly difficult tasks, often independently once they've received their initial instructions. Based on that, we can expect AI to follow a path similar to the ones previously charted by technologies such as electricity, telecommunications, and the internet: evolving from a novelty we marvel at to an engine of rapid growth, and ultimately becoming an essential utility. Putting aside $200 per month adds up to $2,400 per year. Do that for just over nine straight years (110 months), and you end up with $22,000 just from contributions. To plot what that might turn into over time, let's look at several paths forward, running from bearish to bullish. At the low end, if Nvidia endures a negative 5% annualized return, you'd end up with a position worth $17,677. On the other hand, the total skyrockets to more than $61,930 with a 20% annualized return. For context, Nvidia has averaged an eye-popping 63% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) over the last 10 years. But given that it's now the world's largest company, accounting for about 7% of the value of the entire U.S. stock market all by itself, it's unreasonable to think that it could repeat that type of performance over the next decade. There are two obvious threats that could put hurdles in the way of Nvidia's growth. First, regardless of demand, the company might not actually be able to source enough components or production capacity to deliver fully on that demand. On the latest earnings call, Huang noted that "our entire supply chain is challenged." Ultimately, Nvidia can only grow as fast as its suppliers and foundry partners allow, and if the supply chain begins to bend and creak under the enormous weight of the AI revolution, that could slow Nvidia's growth. NVDA Revenue (Quarterly YoY Growth) data by YCharts. Second, Nvidia's customers and competitors (which in some cases are the same companies) might alter their courses. AI hyperscalers are spending enormous amounts of money building out AI infrastructure at breakneck speed. If one or more were to pull back on spending, Nvidia's top line could take a hit. Similarly, rising competition could begin to erode Nvidia's margins. Direct rivals like AMD are gaining ground with new products, and even Nvidia's largest customers like Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft are investing heavily in developing their own AI chips in partnership with players like Broadcom and Marvell Technology. For argument's sake, let's say that Nvidia could deliver a 10% annualized return over the next 110 months. At that rate, the total value of your position would grow to just over $35,000. This growth rate assumes Nvidia will face continued supply chain challenges, but not catastrophic ones. It also assumes that, even as competition continues to increase, Nvidia will maintain a significant competitive advantage in data center processors. In summary, the $200/month habit is entirely controllable; the results are not. Nonetheless, a person who consistently invests is already paying their future self and is likely to be rewarded. Even if Nvidia falls well short of its recent returns, a market-matching 10% return would still deliver significant benefits. Jake Lerch has positions in Alphabet, Amazon, and Nvidia. title: Tom Lee Says AI Selloff Is Nearing Its End, Points To Setup Similar To Cisco's 1997 Rout — Sees Opportunity In NVDA, Software And Beyond - TradingView
content: Fundstrat Managing Partner Tom Lee on Friday said that he sees the recent selloff in AI stocks as an opportunity rather than the start of a deeper unwind. During an interview with CNBC, Lee argued that several of the pressures weighing on technology stocks are beginning to ease now. His comments come amid a sharp selloff in tech stocks, with the Nasdaq Composite falling 2.6% on Thursday, suffering its worst single-day decline since June. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) also fell 6% and 7% respectively on Thursday, their biggest single-day declines since June. Lee Dismisses Concerns, Says Selloff Is Nearing Its End Lee dismissed concerns of a broader decline in tech stocks, saying that he would buy the dip. “I think we’re near the end stages of the sell off because it’s become a consensus short to be shorting tech,” Lee said. The strategist pointed to a shift in the interest-rate backdrop as one reason for his optimism. Treasury yields have moved back below 5% after investors had worried that rates could climb toward 6%, while Lee said the Federal Reserve could be “flipping potentially dovish.” At the same time, he argued that the weakness in technology stocks does not necessarily signal that the underlying AI investment cycle is breaking down. “We’re continuing to see astounding discoveries made by AI,” Lee said, arguing that concerns surrounding AI are actually helping prevent the market from becoming a speculative bubble. He also pointed to tighter debt markets as a restraint on excessive speculation. “I think it’s actually a very healthy correction that way,” Lee said, arguing that constrained financing is preventing a “runaway speculative boom.” Lee Sees Cisco-Like Setup, Likes Nvidia And Software Lee compared the current environment with the late-1990s technology market, specifically pointing to Cisco Systems Inc.'s (CSCO) sharp decline in 1997 before the networking giant resumed its advance. He pointed out that Cisco experienced a major drawdown during this period as investors grappled with concerns over monetary policy and the sustainability of technology valuations. Lee added that a sharp correction did not prevent the broader technology investment cycle from continuing. Lee believes that the current cycle is similar to the one he mentioned above, adding that he sees opportunities in companies addressing AI infrastructure bottlenecks, memory stocks, Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) and the “Magnificent Seven”. “I think the AI and the bottlenecks are the memories and the Nvidia’s and the Mag 7. They’re being sold because it is easy to short them now,” he said. Beyond the major AI hardware names, Lee said he also likes software and cryptocurrency, while adding that there is potential for a broader cyclical move. Lee also argued that the AI infrastructure buildout remains enormous, estimating $30 trillion in spends over the next 25 years. He said the scale could ultimately make AI a more important infrastructure investment than previous major technology buildouts. During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, gained 0.15%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) edged up by 0.07%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) rose 0.13%. Apple Inc.’s (AAPL) $2,200 iPhone Duo appears to be getting off to a stronger start than Wall Street anticipated, with long lines at Apple stores on launch day prompting longtime Apple watcher Gene Munster to raise his confidence in the device’s sales prospects. Munster, managing partner at Deepwater Asset Management, expects Apple to sell 20 million iPhone Duo units in fiscal 2027, well above Wall Street’s roughly 12 million-unit estimate. He said the higher-priced device could become a meaningful contributor to Apple’s overall iPhone growth. Apple shares ended with a decline of 0.1% in Friday’s regular trade, edged lower by 0.03% in the afterhours session. Munster said his initial observations from Apple stores on launch morning strengthened his conviction in his 20 million-unit forecast, which would represent roughly 7% of total iPhone unit sales in FY27. The forecast compares with the Street’s expectation of around 12 million units. Munster noted that the difference of roughly eight million incremental units could add about 3% to overall iPhone growth in FY27. The bigger factor, however, is the iPhone Duo’s significantly higher selling price. Munster estimates that the additional customers would be moving from an iPhone with an average selling price of about $1,200 to the $2,200 Duo. That combination could add approximately $8 billion to the Street’s current FY27 iPhone revenue estimate of $279 billion, according to Munster. Munster’s bullishness comes despite the Duo’s relatively higher price compared to other iPhones. The investor pointed to shorter launch-day lines compared with the iPhone XS and XS Max launch in 2018, but argued that the comparison needs to account for the Duo’s much higher price. He noted that the iPhone Duo’s price is about 82% higher than the iPhone XS Max was at launch. As a result, Munster views the combination of fewer buyers and significantly higher revenue per device as evidence of a solid start rather than a weak one. Wall Street currently expects the Duo to remain a niche product, accounting for about 4% of iPhone units and 7% of iPhone revenue in FY27. Munster is considerably more bullish, projecting the device will represent 8% of units and 16% of revenue. He expects Apple’s overall iPhone business to grow 13% in FY27, compared with the Street’s 10% forecast, with the Duo providing part of that lift. Looking further ahead, he sees the device contributing even more meaningfully to the iPhone lineup in FY28. Last week, analysts at Evercore ISI noted that iPhone Duo delivery dates quickly stretched to late January across tracked regions and configurations, calling the demand signal “solidly out of the gate” while cautioning that supply constraints could also be contributing. Munster similarly said lead times stabilizing around Jan. 25 increased his confidence in a 20 million-unit FY27 forecast, though he acknowledged Apple’s production capacity remains unknown. The investor also noted that iPhone 18 Pro lead times have cooled, while Pro Max demand has held up better. According to a Reuters report citing sources familiar with the matter, the requests by both administrations included expanding the availability of Starlink services in Ukraine and Iran, while restricting access to Iran-backed groups in the Middle East. SpaceX shares gained nearly 2% in Friday’s regular trading session, and edged up by 0.1% further during the afterhours trade. According to the report, officials in the two administrations shared intelligence with SpaceX indicating that the groups had obtained diverted Starlink terminals through intermediaries. The terminals were subsequently deactivated in some cases, the report noted. The Biden administration also pushed SpaceX to expand Starlink access for Ukraine after Russia's invasion in 2022. The Biden administration separately asked SpaceX to activate Starlink in Iran during protests in the country, with the U.S. government helping move Starlink terminals into Iran. The Trump administration reportedly made similar requests following U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran in 2025 and 2026. Trump officials discussed with Musk and SpaceX getting Starlink terminals into Iran and activating them to improve internet access and communications for anti-government protesters. This comes amid concerns that SpaceX’s Starlink services have been slowed down in Ukraine. Last week, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said the restrictions had affected military drones, while reports suggested that the order to throttle Starshield came from inside the White House. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has maintained that SpaceX-powered Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the U.S. government and that decisions on speed or usage ultimately rest with the U.S. military and the president. Amid this, Trump told reporters on Friday that while he believes that the Starlink throttling issue over Ukraine has been fixed, he would speak to Musk if that is not the case. Crude oil prices have climbed to a six-month high as escalating attacks and rising tensions in the Middle East add to concerns about energy supply disruptions. The latest escalation comes as fighting involving the Iran-aligned Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition has intensified, while shipping incidents have added to concerns around key waterways used to transport oil. Goldman Sachs' co-head of Global Commodities Research and head of Oil Research, Daan Struyven, said the recent rise in crude prices reflects growing downside risks to supply, with physical buyers and investors both contributing to the stronger market. Crude oil prices rose to a six-month high, with the U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures expiring in December rising 4.46% to $103.44 a barrel after a 7.81% gain the week before. Brent crude futures expiring in December rose 6.24% this week, hovering around $116.93 a barrel after a 4.91% increase the week before. The United States Oil Fund ETF (USO) rose more than 4% on Friday, while the ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil ETF (UCO) gained about 4%. Struyven said Brent crude had risen sharply as growing Middle East tensions and increasing downside risks to supply prompted buyers to bid up barrels in both physical and financial markets. According to Struyven, refiners are among those buying more crude because of the intensification of shipping attacks and strikes on infrastructure by the Houthis. With inventories low, physical buyers are trying to secure barrels while they remain available. Struyven said refiners see a "high probability of a sharp drop in supply," helping explain the precautionary buying taking place in the physical oil market. He also pointed to financial-market demand, saying investors are buying oil as a hedge against higher energy prices because bonds and equities have become unusually sensitive to movements in crude. Goldman Sachs sees the risks to oil prices as increasingly symmetrical following the recent surge, although Struyven said risks to the firm's forecasts remain skewed to the upside. The bank's base case calls for Brent to end this year at $90 a barrel and average $80 a barrel in 2027. Struyven identified an intensification of shipping attacks, damage to oil infrastructure and a more persistent risk premium as key upside risks. The analyst highlighted that crude oil exports from the Persian Gulf had reached about 110% of 2025 average levels over the previous couple of weeks, while refined-product exports such as diesel were running at only about 40% of the 2025 average. He attributed part of the disparity to damage to refineries in the Middle East and the greater difficulty of arranging ship-to-ship transfers for refined products. Goldman Sachs also sees factors beyond the Middle East supporting refined-product prices. Struyven pointed to structural tightness stemming from years of underinvestment, as well as reduced diesel production at Russian refineries following Ukrainian drone attacks. Tensions around key Middle East shipping routes have intensified in recent weeks, with attacks involving the Iran-aligned Houthis adding to concerns over the movement of oil and other energy products. According to a Reuters report, Saudi Aramco ordered the evacuation of its headquarters in Dhahran on Thursday, as fighting intensified between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis. Dhahran is located near Bahrain and is home to the headquarters of the world's largest crude oil exporter. Separately, an oil spill was detected off the coast of Umm Al Quwain in the United Arab Emirates, according to the UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment. The ministry did not say what caused the spill, and authorities had not identified the tanker involved. Both tech leaders have been handsomely rewarded for their troubles. Over the past five years, Nvidia's shares have climbed by about 904%, as of writing, while Broadcom has gained 563%. Both could continue capitalizing on the AI industry's growth, but which one will perform better over the next five years? My money is on Nvidia, and here is why. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » Nvidia is best known for making GPUs (graphics processing units), the workhorse of AI training. Demand for the company's products has been the main driver behind outstanding revenue and earnings growth in recent years. However, many worry that this tailwind may be coming to an end. There is increased demand for Application-Specific Integrated Circuits, custom AI chips designed to handle specific workloads. Broadcom is a leader in designing ASICs. As companies increasingly seek to reduce their reliance on Nvidia's hardware for various reasons, including price-related ones, Broadcom may benefit. Even so, several things signal that demand for Nvidia's GPUs will remain high for the foreseeable future. For instance, even as some of the hyperscalers double down on AI chips, they remain loyal Nvidia customers. Some of them have said so. Amazon's (NASDAQ:AMZN) CEO, Andy Jassy, predicted that the company would be an Nvidia partner for as long as he can foresee. Other companies, including Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) and Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX), are spending fortunes on their AI-related ambitions. So, it appears that the predicted continued increase in AI infrastructure spending will benefit Nvidia over the medium term. It should benefit Broadcom as well, but there are several reasons Nvidia is arguably in a better position. Let's consider three of them. First, Nvidia is the undisputed leader in the GPU market, holding a more than 90% market share. The company's technological expertise is only part of the reason it has remained the top player in this industry. Its real competitive edge stems from its CUDA ecosystem, which creates high switching costs. Broadcom is also a leader in the ASIC space, but its roughly 60% market share isn't nearly as impressive as Nvidia's dominance in GPUs. Besides, I'd argue that Broadcom's moat is narrower, while the company is increasingly facing tough competition. Second, even as Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue continues to grow rapidly, this business has lower gross margins than the company's Infrastructure software segment. So, as AI semiconductor revenue accounts for an increasingly large percentage of revenue, gross margins could drop. That won't mean lower profits. It will mean a lower gross profit per dollar of revenue. Third, Nvidia is no longer just a GPU company. The company has expanded well beyond that and now offers a full-stack AI platform. The company's GPU business should remain the main growth driver, but other products, such as CPUs (central processing units), should contribute meaningfully over the medium term. It is true that Broadcom is significantly diversified beyond its semiconductor solutions, notably thanks to its software segment. But Nvidia has also made an effort to diversify its business, and that could pay rich dividends down the road. Which one of these two companies appears more attractively valued right now? Some might say it is Broadcom. It is trading at 19.4x forward earnings, versus Nvidia's 24.9x, and an average of 19.3x for information technology stocks. I'd buy Broadcom's shares at current levels, but Nvidia looks more attractive given its position in the AI industry and therefore deserves a higher premium. Both companies are benefiting from rising AI infrastructure investments, but their growth opportunities, valuations and risks differ. With NVIDIA trading at a lower price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple and Lam Research delivering stronger year-to-date stock gains, which semiconductor stock offers investors a better buying opportunity today? Data Center revenues surged 117% to $89 billion, driven by strong demand for its Blackwell Ultra infrastructure. However, NVIDIA faces significant challenges. Supply constraints are limiting its ability to meet customer demand, while rising memory costs are expected to pressure gross margins. Management anticipates margins could decline to 71–72% in the fourth quarter before recovering to 72–73% in fiscal 2028. Geopolitical uncertainty also remains a concern, with the company's forward outlook assuming no Data Center compute revenues from China. Despite these risks, NVIDIA's strong profitability, computing ecosystem and expanding customer base support its long-term investment appeal. Lam Research is benefiting from growing semiconductor manufacturing requirements as AI chips, high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and advanced packaging become increasingly complex. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, revenues increased 54.4% year over year to $8.22 billion. Its customer support business provides another growth driver, generating nearly $2.5 billion in quarterly revenues. Management expects calendar year 2026 systems revenues to increase well more than 40% and projects wafer fabrication equipment spending to exceed $200 billion in 2027. Nevertheless, Lam Research remains exposed to semiconductor capital-spending cycles. Clean-room availability and component shortages are restricting industry output, and near-term constraints limited its second-quarter revenue guidance to $8.6 billion, plus or minus $400 million. The revenue guidance reflects a 4.6% sequential increase, significantly lower than the 22.3% increase in the second quarter. China supplied 35% of first-quarter revenues, but management expects a meaningfully lower share in the second quarter. These factors could affect near-term growth. Analysts’ projections suggest NVDA has a better growth profile than LRCX. NVIDIA has the valuation advantage, trading at a forward 12-month P/E multiple of 15.18 compared with 23.02 for Lam Research. This difference is notable, given NVIDIA's faster recent revenue growth, higher gross margins and strong revenue outlook. Lam Research has delivered superior stock market momentum, with shares rising 33.4% year to date compared with a 13.8% gain for NVIDIA. However, NVDA's lower valuation and stronger growth profile make it more attractive than LRCX. Lam Research offers compelling exposure to rising semiconductor manufacturing spending, advanced packaging and memory production. Its record profitability and favorable industry outlook make it a strong contender. However, NVIDIA appears to be the better investment bet today. Its faster growth, 75% gross margin, expanding AI customer base and lower P/E multiple offer a more attractive mix of growth and relative value. Supply constraints, memory costs and geopolitical risks remain important considerations, but NVIDIA's leadership in AI computing gives it the edge. The recommendations of Wall Street analysts are often relied on by investors when deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock. Media reports about these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts changing their ratings often affect a stock's price. Do they really matter, though? Before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage, let's see what these Wall Street heavyweights think about Nvidia (NVDA). Nvidia currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.13, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 53 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.13 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy. Of the 53 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 49 are Strong Buy and three are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 92.5% and 5.7% of all recommendations. Check price target & stock forecast for Nvidia here>>> While the ABR calls for buying Nvidia, it may not be wise to make an investment decision solely based on this information. Several studies have shown limited to no success of brokerage recommendations in guiding investors to pick stocks with the best price increase potential. Are you wondering why? The vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover often results in a strong positive bias of their analysts in rating it. Our research shows that for every "Strong Sell" recommendation, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations. In other words, their interests aren't always aligned with retail investors, rarely indicating where the price of a stock could actually be heading. Therefore, the best use of this information could be validating your own research or an indicator that has proven to be highly successful in predicting a stock's price movement. Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. Therefore, using the ABR to validate the Zacks Rank could be an efficient way of making a profitable investment decision. In spite of the fact that Zacks Rank and ABR both appear on a scale from 1 to 5, they are two completely different measures. The ABR is calculated solely based on brokerage recommendations and is typically displayed with decimals (example: 1.28). In contrast, the Zacks Rank is a quantitative model allowing investors to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5. It has been and continues to be the case that analysts employed by brokerage firms are overly optimistic with their recommendations. Because of their employers' vested interests, these analysts issue more favorable ratings than their research would support, misguiding investors far more often than helping them. In contrast, the Zacks Rank is driven by earnings estimate revisions. And near-term stock price movements are strongly correlated with trends in earnings estimate revisions, according to empirical research. In addition, the different Zacks Rank grades are applied proportionately to all stocks for which brokerage analysts provide current-year earnings estimates. In other words, this tool always maintains a balance among its five ranks. Another key difference between the ABR and Zacks Rank is freshness. The ABR is not necessarily up-to-date when you look at it. But, since brokerage analysts keep revising their earnings estimates to account for a company's changing business trends, and their actions get reflected in the Zacks Rank quickly enough, it is always timely in indicating future price movements. Looking at the earnings estimate revisions for Nvidia, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 0.6% over the past month to $9.3. Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason for the stock to soar in the near term. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) for Nvidia. title: NVDA vs. LRCX: Which AI Semiconductor Stock Is the Better Buy? - Yahoo Finance UK
content: Tip: Try a valid symbol or a specific company name for relevant results NVIDIA Corporation NVDA and Lam Research Corporation LRCX are two leading semiconductor stocks benefiting from the artificial intelligence (AI) boom. NVIDIA powers AI workloads through its advanced computing chips and platforms, while Lam Research provides essential manufacturing equipment used to produce advanced chips and memory. Both companies are benefiting from rising AI infrastructure investments, but their growth opportunities, valuations and risks differ. With NVIDIA trading at a lower price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple and Lam Research delivering stronger year-to-date stock gains, which semiconductor stock offers investors a better buying opportunity today? Let's find out. NVIDIA delivered an impressive second-quarter fiscal 2027 performance, with revenues soaring 106% year over year to $96.22 billion. Data Center revenues surged 117% to $89 billion, driven by strong demand for its Blackwell Ultra infrastructure. Non-GAAP earnings per share (EPS) increased 120% to $2.22, while gross margin reached 75%. NVIDIA Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | NVIDIA Corporation Quote NVIDIA's growth opportunities extend beyond hyperscalers to AI cloud providers, enterprises and sovereign customers. The rollout of its Vera Rubin platform and expanding AI infrastructure investments could support further growth. Its third-quarter revenue guidance of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, and management's preliminary expectation of roughly 70% fiscal 2028 growth signal continued momentum. However, NVIDIA faces significant challenges. Supply constraints are limiting its ability to meet customer demand, while rising memory costs are expected to pressure gross margins. Management anticipates margins could decline to 71–72% in the fourth quarter before recovering to 72–73% in fiscal 2028. Geopolitical uncertainty also remains a concern, with the company's forward outlook assuming no Data Center compute revenues from China. Despite these risks, NVIDIA's strong profitability, computing ecosystem and expanding customer base support its long-term investment appeal. Lam Research is benefiting from growing semiconductor manufacturing requirements as AI chips, high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and advanced packaging become increasingly complex. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, revenues increased 54.4% year over year to $8.22 billion. Non-GAAP EPS rose 74.6% to $2.20, while non-GAAP gross and operating margins reached records of 52.4% and 40.2%, respectively. Lam Research Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Lam Research Corporation Quote The company's deposition and etch technologies are essential to manufacturing advanced semiconductors. Its customer support business provides another growth driver, generating nearly $2.5 billion in quarterly revenues. Management expects calendar year 2026 systems revenues to increase well more than 40% and projects wafer fabrication equipment spending to exceed $200 billion in 2027. Nevertheless, Lam Research remains exposed to semiconductor capital-spending cycles. Clean-room availability and component shortages are restricting industry output, and near-term constraints limited its second-quarter revenue guidance to $8.6 billion, plus or minus $400 million. The revenue guidance reflects a 4.6% sequential increase, significantly lower than the 22.3% increase in the second quarter. China supplied 35% of first-quarter revenues, but management expects a meaningfully lower share in the second quarter. These factors could affect near-term growth. Analysts' projections suggest NVDA has a better growth profile than LRCX. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for NVIDIA's fiscal 2027 revenues and EPS indicates a year-over-year increase of 88.7% and 95%, respectively. For fiscal 2028, the consensus marks for revenue and EPS suggest year-over-year growth of 67.5% and 69.3%, respectively. Meanwhile, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for Lam Research's fiscal 2027 revenues and EPS indicates a year-over-year jump of 48.5% and 60.9%, respectively. For fiscal 2028, the consensus marks for revenue and EPS suggest year-over-year growth of 17.2% and 22.2%, respectively. NVIDIA has the valuation advantage, trading at a forward 12-month P/E multiple of 15.18 compared with 23.02 for Lam Research. This difference is notable, given NVIDIA's faster recent revenue growth, higher gross margins and strong revenue outlook. Lam Research has delivered superior stock market momentum, with shares rising 33.4% year to date compared with a 13.8% gain for NVIDIA. However, NVDA's lower valuation and stronger growth profile make it more attractive than LRCX. Lam Research offers compelling exposure to rising semiconductor manufacturing spending, advanced packaging and memory production. Its record profitability and favorable industry outlook make it a strong contender. However, NVIDIA appears to be the better investment bet today. Its faster growth, 75% gross margin, expanding AI customer base and lower P/E multiple offer a more attractive mix of growth and relative value. Supply constraints, memory costs and geopolitical risks remain important considerations, but NVIDIA's leadership in AI computing gives it the edge. Currently, NVIDIA sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), making it a must-pick compared with Lam Research, which has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). title: Nasdaq, Dow, S&P 500 Futures Drop Premarket: NVDA, AMD, META, CRWV, MRNA, WDC, BE In Focus - TradingView
content: U.S. stock futures were lower early on Friday after a sharp sell-off in chip stocks, as concerns grew that the artificial intelligence trade could lose near-term momentum. As of 6 a.m. ET, Nasdaq 100 futures edged 0.04% lower, while Dow futures fell 0.60%. S&P 500 futures tumbled 0.23%. Earlier, on Thursday, the benchmark indexes ended mixed, with the S&P 500 down 1.2%, the Nasdaq 100 falling 2.9%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average remaining flat. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits remained weak. Sentiment toward the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500, trended in ‘extremely bearish’ territory over the past day. The Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq 100, saw sentiment shift to ‘bearish’ from ‘extremely bearish’, while sentiment towards the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) remained in the ‘extremely bearish’ zone. Oil prices rose again amid escalating geopolitical tensions, with reports suggesting that the U.S. and Israel are considering fresh strikes on Iran after the U.S. midterm elections in November. Tehran has vowed to retaliate against any new attacks, potentially targeting economic and civilian infrastructure, the Wall Street Journal reported. As of 6 a.m. ET, Brent crude futures expiring December were up 1.1% to $114 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures gained 1.6% % to over $101 per barrel. Meta Platforms (META): Shares dipped 0.6% in early premarket trading on Friday, recovering slightly after falling more than 7% on Thursday, when investors reacted negatively to another increase in the company’s annual AI spending forecast and plans to issue new shares to help fund the investment. The sell-off came despite better-than-expected results and a strong forecast, highlighting investor concerns about the scale of AI investments and the prospect of even cash-rich technology companies taking on debt to finance them. Nvidia (NVDA): The stock edged 0.4% higher in early premarket trading on Friday after ending Thursday’s regular session 4.4% down. Adding to concerns over Meta’s rising AI spending, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC that “there is a scarcity of capital” for AI infrastructure, adding that “the demand for capital is much greater than the availability.” Advanced Micro Devices (AMD): Shares gained nearly 1% in early premarket trading on Friday, recovering some ground after ending Thursday’s session more than 8% lower. Like Meta Platforms and Nvidia, AMD was attempting a rebound after a sharp sell-off in AI-related stocks in the previous session. CoreWeave (CRWV): The stock was up 2% in premarket trading on Friday after hitting a fresh 17-month low of $53.50 during Thursday’s session. Concerns over mounting debt and broader weakness in the AI sector have weighed on the stock. Despite the premarket gains, CRWV was on track for a third straight week of losses as rising borrowing costs and concerns about slowing AI demand continued to weigh on sentiment. SK Hynix (SKHY): Shares rose almost 5% in premarket trading on Friday. The stock closed 4.4% higher on Thursday, reversing earlier losses of around 3% after the chipmaker halted its review of potential pre-IPO fundraising and listing options for its U.S. subsidiary, Solidigm. According to CNBC, Josh Gilbert, lead analyst for APAC at investment platform eToro, said the recovery suggested concerns over a potential Solidigm IPO had weighed on investor sentiment. Moderna Inc. (MRNA): Shares fell over 4% in premarket trading on Friday, after Moderna’s cancer-vaccine rally hit a setback on Thursday. MRNA is heading for its worst weekly performance in three months, while Mizuho analyst Jared Holz warned that extreme volatility had made the stock a “do-not-trade” for many investors. On Thursday, the shares plunged nearly 18% to close at $202.63, marking their steepest single-day decline in more than two months. Western Digital Corp. (WDC): The stock was down around 2% in premarket trading despite the company beating fiscal first-quarter earnings expectations. The hard-drive maker delivered stronger profits and an upbeat second-quarter outlook, addressing concerns that the storage boom was losing momentum. However, the upbeat results failed to lift sentiment. Bloom Energy Corp. (BE): Bloom Energy Corp. (BE): Shares of the fuel cell maker dropped as much as 2% in premarket trading on Friday after plunging nearly 9% on Thursday and extending losses overnight. The sell-off followed its third-quarter results, which raised concerns over capital expenditure and cash flow. Other tickers trending on Stocktwits at the time of writing included Nokia (NOK), Walmart (WMT) and Charles Schwab (SCHW). On the economic front, traders will watch for the final University of Michigan consumer sentiment reading. Meanwhile, American Express Co. (AXP) and Schlumberger Ltd.
